metadata.topic: Quantitative Chemistry — Molar Concentration from Solubility

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q1g — Concentration of Saturated KNO₃ at 35°C
question.text:
From the solubility graph, the solubility of potassium nitrate (KNO₃) at 35°C is approximately 48 g per 100 cm³ of water.

Calculate the concentration in mol dm⁻³ of a saturated solution of potassium nitrate at 35°C.

R.A.M.: K = 39, N = 14, O = 16
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Step 1: Molar mass of KNO₃ = 39 + 14 + 3(16) = 39 + 14 + 48 = 101 g mol⁻¹
Step 2: Moles of KNO₃ in 48 g = 48 ÷ 101 = 0.475 mol
Step 3: Convert volume to dm³: 100 cm³ = 0.1 dm³
Step 4: Concentration = moles ÷ volume = 0.475 ÷ 0.1 = 4.75 mol dm⁻³

Common errors: Forgetting to divide by volume (0.1 dm³ not 100 cm³); using wrong molar mass for KNO₃.

steps.label:
Given: Solubility of KNO₃ at 35°C = 48 g per 100 cm³  |  RAM: K = 39, N = 14, O = 16
Formula: c (mol dm⁻³) = n / V    n = mass ÷ molar mass    100 cm³ = 0.1 dm³
Calculate the molar mass of KNO₃. (1 mark)
Calculate the moles of KNO₃ in 48 g. (1 mark)
Calculate the concentration in mol dm⁻³. (2 marks)

fields.label: Molar mass of KNO₃ = _____ g mol⁻¹

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Molar mass = K + N + 3×O = 39 + 14 + 48 = 101 g/mol. Don't forget oxygen has 3 atoms in NO₃⁻.
n = 48 ÷ 101 = 0.475 mol. Divide the mass of KNO₃ by its molar mass.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass. n = 48 ÷ 101 = 0.475 mol.

fields.label: Volume in dm³ = _____ dm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: Convert 100 cm³ to dm³: divide by 1000. 100 ÷ 1000 = 0.1 dm³

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³. So 100 cm³ ÷ 1000 = 0.1 dm³. You must convert before calculating concentration.
c = moles ÷ volume (in dm³) = 0.475 ÷ 0.1 = 4.75 mol dm⁻³.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Concentration (mol/dm³) = moles ÷ volume (dm³). Make sure volume is in dm³, not cm³.
